review:
The OG version played a lot better and, while slower paced, was more fun and had more build variety combative tension in the mechanics. In the current design meta every character has everything unlocked so games are lightning fast dead-man-walking scenarios if any team has any vague DPS edge due to AOEs or lock downs or both. Certain character types such as supports have no actual purpose in this meta as they can't do their actual job effectively enough as they only become viable relative directly to how many unlocks they get over time.

The Creeps may as well not exist now. They are easily defeated since every ability is unlocked at the start of the match, thus they no longer serve any purpose or pose any distinct threat or objective focus. In the OG game there was a very specific risk-reward tension around fighting the creeps and keeping them at bay as a sort of lite PvE objective mission while weaving in and out of PvP conflicts to build resources or to carefully push enemies back. Now PvP is constant as creeps are entirely a non-threat or meaningful objective like they used to be.

Some characters are entirely broken by having both abilities unlocked at the start, while others, since there is no time to build resources to buy upgrades, are deadlocked. Certain characters were always underpowered by design since they were supports, but now they are entirely useless with no upsides as they will never have time to get decent upgrades to make themselves decently threatening against most opponents.

I was expecting more from the revived version of this game, but sticking to the new ruleset/meta was a huge mistake and makes the game frustrating to play and actively unfun and tedious to experience unless you play a specific handful of characters who have no real downsides.

This game genuinely was fun and engaging in its early years. The new meta feels like a spiteful insult to the 132 hours I enjoyed in the original game. As if that game never existed.

The remains of what was once a wonderful game. Core memories were formed playing this niche title, but the game hasn't been touched in any real capacity in several years. To top it off, what little remains of the community is exceedingly toxic and unwelcoming to newer players, actively ruining what little there is left to experience. It saddens me to say that the game is well and truly dead.

Throwing a positive review because the game is still great. Been playing since the game was (mandatory) $10 and had maybe 10 characters tops and like 3 maps. Some important notes for new and old players:

The developer, Ronimo Games, went bankrupt, BUT Atari brought the servers back to the most recent version of the game + a new update. Atari is under new management and has been pushing good business practices. The irony of a modern game developer going out of business trying to develop some kind of co-op, live service game to have some level of passive income when they already had a very good, live-service game is absurd. This was one of the 3 MOBAs I have put more than 30 hours into, and I haven't touched Dota 2 since 2013, with Heroes of the Storm sucking up most of my time. So it was a shame that the game was dead (literally) for a while.

All the mixed reviews were from ages ago, when the servers were gone or the game had cheaters/sweatlords. Just got out of a game (2 matches back-to-back) and it was very fun, feels balanced enough. There was no landslide victory. This is still a MOBA, so I would suggest trying to get comfortable with a character and the controls, but it's much easier to learn than any other MOBA. I didn't have to look at a meta guide.

There is no skill-based matchmaking algorithm, there is no dopamine FOMO element, and buying all the characters is $20 total. If that sounds good to you, it is worth your time to play it for free and see if you enjoy it. 3 on 3 has fast queue times, no matter the playerbase. You are still going to run into very good players, so I would suggest picking a ranged hero + support class for new players so they can keep distance. Voltar is very fun, I love Voltar. Please, more Voltar.

I have been heavily invested in PC gaming and Steam since around 2011/2012 (with my first PC in 2005), and I can honestly say that nothing like Awesomenauts has come out since; it's so damn good. The era of an indie company/smaller studio releasing a multiplayer-only game that retains a strong following post-launch (not just flavor of the month) without FOMO and dopamine spikes, while also having amazing gameplay (Natural Selection 2, Section 8, Awesomenauts, etc) is dead, but we can still enjoy at least ONE of these titles thanks to Atari and the communities who still play them.

Awesomenauts is a 2D, side-scrolling MOBA. It has tens of unique, playable characters with their own skills and weaknesses. Years of updates have lead to a pretty balanced game. The graphic style is colourful and unique and this game has a very good soundtrack. Since they made it free to play there are more then enough players. unfortunately there remain some connection issues from time to time. Overall great game.

Replayability: As of writing this review, Awesomenauts has stolen over 750 hours of my free time, and it is bound to rob me for many years to come. With the multiple match ups (meaning how good certain characters are against other certain characters, on a scale of equal player skill) no session has ever felt the same.

Arenas: I cannot compare it to the likes of DOTA or LoL, since I havent played either, but coming from someone whos played the likes of Powerstone 2 for the Dreamcast, I can tell you that this game offers a robust experience. The arenas are structured in such a way that allow you to go miles by taking an inch. 

Characters: The prime beef. Ronimo takes a bit of slack when it comes to balancing certain character traits and abilities, half of which I would say are very much deserved, but at the end of the day using the character in a way that outplays your opponents strengths and capitalizes on there weaknesses will outrule any match up against you. You are bound to find a character, if not half the cast, to your liking~

Single Player: There is none. This game will not engage you if not played online. Future DLC will patch in alot of match customizablity, so I cant say much on how they will integrate it, but not including the Starstorm DLC, I would not reccomend this game to anyone who is timid of the online environment.

Art: The game is advertised to look and sound like a Saturday morning cartoon. The Musical Score matches this, with catchy rhythmic beats that loop in the background and character specific that play ala reward for killing sprees. The graphics, not so much. Dont get me wrong, the sprites are colorful (albiet small in relation to everything else on screen, but still packed with personality) and the levels looks gorgously bright and tell a story, but the only thing "Saturday Cartoon" about it is the intro video and character portraits. Still, you get what you get, and if youre a fan of the child friendly art style, you wont be disappointed.

Awesomenauts is a combination of 2D platform/side-scroller with a MOBA (3v3), which creates an interesting combination that turns out as a very enjoyable experience for people who are fond of both genres. Like most 2D platforms,  the main mechanics are simple and it's very intuitive, which makes it easy to learn the basics of the game. It's also similar to 2D platforms in how fast-paced it is, and how much it values reaction times.  However, it also has some of the depth of MOBAs; there are several characters to choose (16 so far and counting), each one with 2 unique abilities and a different set of possible upgrades to choose for your builds and item routes. This combination results in a game that's simple yet fast and competitive. 

In regards to some specific contents of the game:

 The developers are active on this game, they produced 15 characters and 4 maps for the base game, plus microtransactions for skins (which doesn't have any impact on the gameplay itself). They'll be releasing an expansion now (currently on beta/early-access) and expand the game from that point on, so if you want to get access to all present and future features (which so far we know are extra characters, maps, spectator mode and custom-setting games), you'll want to buy both the base game and expansion, which is actually really cheap if you buy it on Steam sales or related stuff. 

The balance of the game is not top-notch but it's pretty good regardless. New players might feel some characters are OP and whatnot, but once you get used to them you'll realise all of them are pretty much playable and none is "game-breaking".

There's a big "luck" factor in the game. Players are not forced to play a full game and teams aren't required to be full to start and continue games (which means you can find yourself alone with 2 bots in your team vs 3 human players, although this doesn't happen often). Players are allowed to leave a game (although they'll be punished by losing ranking points), this happens very frequently, specially on losing teams, which can be a pain in the ass for both teams (losing teams with bots frequently have no chance of winning, on the other side, you can be on a winning team and new players will join the game and make a comeback).  You don't know the map you'll be playing either, which is a problem because some characters have a bigger advantage on certain maps. You don't know what characters the enemy picked either. There's no separated queue for premades and solo players, which is also annoying for a lot of people.

The game netcode is p2p (so, no servers), this is annoying for a lot of players because you won't experience "input lag" (any actions you'll perform will be instantaneous in your screen), but you will experience a delay in actions of other players (basically you'll see that other enemies will hit you even when it looked like you were out of their attack/skill range). This means that you'll need to deduce the enemy intentions beforehand and estimate the true range of abilities and attacks on your screen based on the player's ping. 

Finding full matches is not a problem, and there's a decent amount of players online at most hours, so don't worry about buying a dead game (at least not yet!). There are a lot of players who'll want to play with you and it's easy to make "queue buddies".

The pool of characters is not as huge as in LoL or DoTA, but all characters have clear differences and they're all fun to play. Character synergy and team-comps are very important and sometimes if you don't pick your character properly you'll find yourself with a team that is incompetent in teamfights or pushing.

All in all, I think awesomenauts is a great concept and a very enjoyable game, specially for it's price. It's far from being a masterpiece because of it's issues, but despite that, it's a great experience and you'll have lots of fun playing it, specially if you play with friends.

If I were to go back in time to 2012 to when this game was released, where it stood out with it's infectious and unique presentation and it’s gleaming potential, I'd do it in a heartbeat. As it is today, almost 11 years after release, It's just about become one of the worst experiences I've ever endured, period.

The game is filled to the brim with childish and toxic individuals that will berate, insult, blame and shame you for not playing to their standards. Many of the same individuals will cease to contribute to your team and report if they feel like you are playing on a level bellow themselves. This also makes learning new characters absolutely anxiety inducing because you know for sure that if you play even a little rough, or don't buy the upgrades deemed 'required' to play the character effectively, you know your team will call you out on it and ultimately blame you for losing the game.

I've even had someone say I should commit suicide because they thought I played Gnaw poorly, even though, considering I was learning the character at the time, I thought I was doing pretty well. That should tell you the level of lethargy that infests this dying community and will ultimately be it's downfall. Moments like this happened constantly and I hope this serves as a major warning to anyone considering picking up this game.

As for the gameplay itself, the simplified 2D platformer MOBA might've been a unique take on a very competitive genre back in 2012, but has since become a mindbogglingly irritating series of insane area denial and burst options that will more than likely 1 shot you for even thinking for a second that you could approach 2 inches forward.

This game is so mechanically bare yet there's far too much to learn and understand for new players to reach a point where they can comfortably join a match without the risk of getting lambasted thoroughly by what must be childish men or literal children.

I would have left this game long ago, but sadly my compulsion to get every achievement in every game I play kept me from leaving sooner. If you're an Achievement Hunter, as one myself, I will tell you right now to look elsewhere. While most of the achievements can be done in private custom games with bots, the prestige achievements will be the hell that keeps you from freeing yourself from this mechanically bare bones game and awful community.

I was fortunate enough to already have prestige 5 before the free to play update changed it to where you had to level up characters individually. Levelling up just 5 characters took me 170 hours, a third of which was queuing in the matchmaking system. I was lucky as hell to have a second monitor to pass the time but this is far too long to be spending time on prestige achievements, let alone a game this mechanically empty.

I look upon this game in contempt, I hope to never ever play a game with a community like this and it's a stark reminder as to why I hate multiplayer games.

My playtime in this game is probably enough to tell you tell that I've really enjoyed it. Awesomenauts is a MOBA played in 2D . I picked the game up a few years ago and I still find the game fun to play.

At the start of a match you pick a character. You have the usual classes you find in MOBA:s, such as rogue, tank, support and so on. Every character has their own set of skills and items you get to pick from at the start of the match. Characters and items are unlocked as you level up your account, which is fairly easy to do and comes naturally as you play. The characters in the game all look great I think and they really fit the flippant feel of the game. 

As always there are some balancing issues for a time after a new character is released, but for the most part the characters are pretty well balanced and only your skills determine how tough a fight is going to be, not bad balancing. You will learn how to play most of the characters pretty quickly although there are some characters that require more practice to master them, as is common in most games like Awesomenauts. It wouldn't be much fun otherwise. 

The ease of learning the basics of the game means that you can get into it pretty quickly and with so many characters with very different playstyles you will want to try them out and in this game you're able to do that in very little time.

Matches usually last about 20-30 minutes and if a player disconnects from the match then another player can immediately jump into the game, which is something that I really like about the matchmaking system in Awesomenauts. The possibility to join ongoing games means that a team where a player disconnects isn't necessarily crippled, as is often the case in other MOBA:s.
 
To win a match your team needs to destroy the enemy team's base. To do that you have to push through one or two lanes where turrets need to be destroyed in order to process further. Nothing out of the ordinary here. Mobility plays a big role in Awesomenauts. Not all characters are fast and not all characters have skills that help them escape. This means that when you play as the slower characters, typically the tanks, you will need some knowledge of the layout of a map in order to be able to escape. The importance of mobility is something I really like about the game.

I think that the larger part of the community is pretty friendly, but that could just be because most players tend to not say anything in matches. Ragequitting is very common (or at least it was back when I still played) but other than that you'll probably not have any problems with other players.

TL;DR: I would definitely recommend Awesomenauts to people who like this kind of games. Just watch a few videos of it and you should be able to tell if you would enjoy it.

I know how funny this opener sounds judging by my playtime but a huge chunk of this time was played many years ago. At that time the game was really fun but over the past years it became apparent that the developers have been having no real vision for its future. To be more precise, in hindsight it seems as if there has never been an underlying game design direction that exceeds shoving Nauts with randomly thrown together kits into the game. 

So this is mostly what the game got up to this point: a lot of new Nauts, some of which have really badly designed kits showing little balance between risk and reward, skill floor and ceiling and strengths in general. After some (usually too long) time the worst outliers get balanced via number or upgrade changes but a lot of the problems baked into their kits remain.

Penny for example was an absolute mess on release with nearly every existing CC in her kit while at the same time being more or less capable of flying and deleting enemies within seconds. Even though the stupidity of this design was obvious and it was pointed out dozens of times on the forums the developers left it in the game for months. At some point, way too late, her ridculous strength was regulated but overall her kit remained the same and still is annoying to play against today.

Another example for weirdly balanced kits is Sentry. At base he is capable of dealing the single strongest hitting burst in the game. Simultaneously for whatever reason this skill is also one of the strongest CCs in the game sucking in every Naut in an area that can't escape with a dash or teleport and keeping them locked in place for Sentry's teammates to follow up. To be fair: the skill is telegraphed and for dealing maximum damage it has to be charged by taking damage. You'd be right thinking that such a Naut should be designed in a way that makes playing offensive and risky rerwarding. Instead Sentry doesn't need to engage with enemies - he can simply charge the skill to its full potential by running in front of an enemy turret. In an effort to double down on this his auto attack is one of the most passive and easy to use ones in the game requiring no commitment but instead rewarding backpedaling and kiting.

These Nauts are just examples, Sentry isn't even close to being the worst offender. I could go on writing about a dozen more Nauts with strangely composed kits and characteristics but there's a lot more that went wrong over the years or wasn't fixed. Leaderboards are useless and buggy as hell. The matchmaking is the biggest mess I've ever encountered in an online game (I'm saying this as someone who played a lot of Hots). Paired with the low amount of active players this will make you yearn for good games that aren't stomping new players or playing against two or three premade League 1 tournament players. 

Maps have been having design problems for years or even since launch like too easily controllable mids or a plain stupid invisibility orb that turns a winning team with a bursty Naut into an unstoppable force. Very few of them were tackled, the biggest one for me personally being how easy stalling games with some Nauts is up to this day. For example Lonestar or Raelynn can single-handedly increase the duration of a round by a two-digit number of minutes by simply denying any possibility for pushes. And once again this doesn't come at the expense of any other strength, they are some of the strongest Nauts in the game even without stalling at all, giving the impression the stalling potential wasn't the result of a conscious design decision but simply the consequence of the combination of a thrown together kit and maps that have no mechanisms to prevent stalling.

Updated conclusion (May 2019): don't play this game. It's full to the brim with awful game design decisions and the developers have abandoned it in a ridiculously unbalanced state.  It's not worth anyone's time anymore. The last three Nauts that were added are an unbalanced mess with laughable kits, showing zero understanding of any aspect of the game whatsoever, effortlessly eclipsing the formerly released Nauts which already were horribly designed.

The way I always try to describe Awesomenauts is as a 2D, action platformer MOBA. Ever since I started playing this game, it's a formula that I truly enjoyed in a way that I didn't enjoy something like LoL of Dota. What sets this game apart, from a mechanical standpoint, is that it has much more emphasis on manual positioning of both characters and skills, and that makes it much more challenging and interesting. Aesthetically it is very stylized and pleasing to see, with bright palets and a very well done soundtrack. The cast of characters is really unique and each has it's own unique skils that make them fun to play. And in my experience, both playing online alone (SoloQ) and coordinated team play are fun. Ronimo is always working on adding new characters, balncing them, and interacting with the community.

The only true drawback from this game, in my opinion, is that the community playing it relatively small for a MOBA, which is a real shame. As a result, matchmaking can be problematic sometimes. Finding a match and filling one relatively quick is almost never a problem, but the problem comes in with the difference in skill level of the players in the games.

I wholeheartily recommend this game to anyone who wants a different spin on a MOBA, wants a fun game to play with friends, or just wants to play a fun game.

I also stream this game semi-frequently if you want to see live gameplay of it: twitch.tv/pyrocheese

Awesomenauts is a  2D Multiplayer Online Battle Arena, MOBA for short.  This game is available for €10, and offers you lots of fun for that price. You don't have to pay for anything else, except when you want to buy skins for the 15 awesomenauts. These skins are pure cosmetic, they won't give you an advantage in-game.
 So, what is this game all about? Well, you play as one of the 15 available awesomenauts and you have to destroy the enemy base. Sounds easy right? Well, to do that you have to fight your way through turrets, robotic minions and of course the other team. At the start of the game you try to earn some 'Solar', the gold of Awesomenauts, and buy upgrades for your awesomenaut with it. Aeesomenauts also doesn't have a laning stage, which means you can be ganked every 30 seconds. After a while, one team will have more upgrades and more Solar than the other team and they will push to the other teams base. And then of course destroy it.

Verdict

[b]Review[/b]:

With close to 1300 hours played over two accounts I used to love this game. A simplistic side scrolling MOBA that's very easy to get into, what's not to like? A lot of time was spent in the game, I made friends and we had lots of fun. Unfortunately, as time passed the flaws of the game were revealed.

This game actually favors people with poor internet connections and if you don't have a bad internet connection you might as well simulate one to gain unfair advantage over your opponents. How is this possible? Due to Ronimo being a small company they can't really supply dedicated servers so they designed the game for p2p networking. You have the option to queue in different regions, same or nearby would be recommended. It doesn't matter though, if someone feels the need to queue worldwide (maybe because lack of players) they can join you no matter what your settings are. It gets frustrating real fast playing an opponent with over 300 ms of latency. They can actually pick a naut that favours their ping to get the upper hand because it gets impossible to dodge certain skills because you can't anticipate where a projectile might be on their screen and before you know it you've been hit. If someone choose to queue worldwide you'd think it'd be more of a challenge for them because of latency but it's really the other way around.

And if they don't have high latency they might have packet loss and that can actually trigger effects on abilities multiple times. There's a naut that has the ability to pull other nauts to him using his tongue, if the player has packet loss he can actually tongue you multiple times and this is very frustrating. His client registers that he hit his ability but the packet was lost and had to be sent again and maybe a few more times.

The design wouldn't be so awful if both players had a say in the matter and dedicated servers would make it even better and actually favor players playing on the right side of the globe.

Networking issues aside, the matchmaking could also use some work. Solo queuing is ok but can be a terrible experience since players can just leave the game without any ramifications. If the player hosting the game crashes and the host migration fails everyone gets a loss. Some maps end in single lanes which makes a choke point and favors nauts that can turtle and just delay the game for as long as possible.

[b]edit[/b]:
[strike]I quit playing this game because it was actually making me rage[/strike]. I still occasionally play the game for the sake of ongoing tournaments and to keep in touch with the friends I made along the way. The game still has flaws, some of them being addressed (slowly). Until all of the major issues have been resolved I will not recommend this game.

It's a lot of fun to play when the stars align, but whenever people lag (be it due to connectivity issues or if it's intentional) it ruins the experience completely.
Good memories, try a $20-40 sequel, you'll find a ton of nostalgic players.

Before Awesomenauts I have played a little bit of LoL and DOTA2. These games have always been a non-go for me : gameplay too slow (point & click, no way to evade stuff, little skill involved), learning curve too high (you have to read plenty of guides before you can get a handle on what are the good builds, what to buy etc..), and their community usually just suck. Ragequitting, flaming, "competitive" players, you name it.

Awesomenauts is the exception.

[h1]Easy learning curve[/h1]

This is what kept me playing during my first hours. I did not have to read guides, or to worry about my build - i was just having fun playing this little game. In a few hours only I had understood the basic mechanics of the game.

[h1]Very fast gameplay[/h1]

Jump, shoot, drop, drop, shoot, oh damn there's someone needing help !
Take the jump pad, dash towards the enemies, thus saving your mate, and then drop down to jungle and escape. Woosh, you nearly died, but you just saved your mate.

Shit, in the mean time droids have pushed. Drop, clear bottom droids, take the jump pad.
Ok, your two buddies are right there in top lane, and you see the 3 enemies standing there. Time to initiate ! You dash, your mates follow, you prevent them from escaping by bodyblocking them while nado'ing.. One is about to espape, you are about to die, but your friend Nibbs just launched her Orb, teleports, and the guy is dead. It's a wipeout. Time to push !

And that's basically what the entire game is like. You have no time to rest. You always have something to do, always on your nerves. The slightest mistake might turn the fate of the game.. But you keep playing, you keep pushing. Until victory (or defeat) is achieved.

[h1]Easy to learn, and yet so hard to master[/h1]

After more than 600 hours in this game, I still did not master 100% of the game.

Each one of the 23 characters has a completely different gameplay. That's 23 playstyles to master.  Out of these 23, I think I'm mastering 8 of them. I still have 15 characters to continue learning.. And that's what keeps me playing, even after 600 hours.

[h1]Epic moments ![/h1]

Be it when you kill someone in air battle, or when you barely escape a gank and manage nevertheless to kill one of them, resulting in a wipeout (all 3 of the enemy team dead) because your team supported you - or when both of your team mates died, but all 3 enemies have low health, and you manage to take them all out..

These kind of moments are so rare in the recent games, that Awesomenauts is a perl just for this sake.

[h1]The cons[/h1]

This game is not perfect though. (no game is)
[list]
[*]The community still have a couple of weird people. The kind of people that are attracted by the "MOBA" and "F2P" labels. Flamers, ragequitters, ...
[*]Matchmaking is not great. But the next big update coming in March should solve this issue.
[*]Peer-to-peer system. You can get hit while you're not supposed to on your screen.
[/list]

[h1]Final Words[/h1]

After two-three long years of Awesomenauts, I thought I might give you my full thoughts about this game, now that we are getting close to the end of the Starstorm DLC development and the new Matchmaking server.

First of all, my feelings toward this game are mostly positive. I love the general gameplay style, it's like Smash Bros meeting MOBAs like Dota and LoL, 2D and stuff.
Music, oh boy, Sonic Picnic has really given their best with the game's soundtrack.
Visuals, they're great, I love the 1980's cartoon style Ronimo has been going for, same goes for the characters and lore in general.
Ronimo keeps updating the game with more characters, visual and gameplay advancements, new features such as new bots you can play with, when not having players in game, new game modes in custom games, skins and announcers. It's the reason the game is still going on for it's 3rd year on Steam, has got PS4 release that is also updated from time to time, and Xbox One -version coming.
Community involvement is great thing with this game, as I myself have made some sort of "career" on YouTube somewhat because of Awesomenauts. We've walked the path of YouTube together for these +2 years. And I thank both this game and it's developers with cooperation :) Also, the community of players might sometimes feel childish etc, but there are a lot of smart people who strive to keep Awesomenauts, well, awesome. We have had some great tournaments and other events, our suggestion for character voice lines, skin and/or character ideas are passed down to the game in one form or another, and in example, Replays have given us options to make more different kinds of gameplay videos to YouTube.

Of course, this game has it's issues. Since Ronimo can't afford to rewrite the netcode for Awesomenauts to enable dedicated servers, players have to deal with P2P, which will cause problems if 1. Player/players have faulty connection and/or 2. players involved are from different countries. Of course you can limit the options your matchmaking queue goes for, but it's a bit flawed until Ronimo implements their new Matchmaking servers around the release of Overdrive expansion (which isn't required to use the matchmaking servers, mind you). Connection problems aren't fixed by that, but at least matchmaking will be more "fair" towards players of different skill levels and you are less likely to be put in a game against players from other side of the world.
Speaking of skill levels, new players might find problems to start the game if they skip beginner missions and jump right into the online games (which is not recommended). Skill level might vary even in the higher leagues of leaderboards, but there are cases that new players quit the game because they don't feel the need of commitment to learn the basics and advanced techniques of the game and it's characters.
Then there's character balance. Some characters are already pretty balanced in a sense, but then there are one's that are doomed to be bad or too good. But, balancing acharacter isn't a walk on a sunshine, it's like stacking a house of cards. One slip and the whole house of cards might collapse, of course, then you have to start over again, but once you get it right, man, it feels satisfying. Even though you're missing couple of cards, which in this game are incoming characters and maps.

But, my likes, which are plenty, clearly overpower the dislikes towards this game, and over 2000 hours in the game, I say that I love this game. I believe that Ronimo can and will strive to make this game stand out and stay alive for a long time, and I'm willing to stay with Ronimo until the day Awesomenauts has to move to a higher plane of existence.

I remember when I first saw this game for sale on the XBLA years ago (I was still a scrubby console gamer back then, please forgive me!), and my initial reaction was ‘Wow, this game looks absolutely dreadful’, I just didn’t get it! Luckily, I played this game on a whim, and I have to say, it blew me away!

But first, a bit about the game, it’s a 2D, 3v3 MOBA, currently consisting of a modest roster of 20 ‘Awesomenauts’ (20 is including the Expansion pack ‘Nauts, of which there are 4), where the goal is to destroy the enemies’ damage dealing, high health turrets, thankfully with the help of small damage absorbing droids, in order to destroy the enemies’ drill core, leading to a victory. Each player picks one of the aforementioned ‘Nauts to play as during the match, each with His/her own unique Autoattack and abilities. There is also a currency in this game called ‘Solar’ which allows you to upgrade your abilities. All of this is in the style of an 80’s Saturday morning cartoon show. Boom.

I love this concept (despite hating it initially :s), the 2D aspect of the game means that it requires a lot of platforming ability in order for you to be good at it, and honestly, it’s a very clever twist to the typical MOBA, and it’s made the game very refreshing for me. The graphics and soundtrack are equally invigorating, with some of my favourites being the character themes and killing sprees.

Additionally, this game isn’t short of diversity. Each ‘Naut brings something new to the table in the form of the aforementioned abilities, so, when you get bored of one character, you can play another for a short while, it never feels like you’re playing the same game twice! Furthermore, upgrades add to this diversity. There are 4 rows of upgrades for your abilities, with 6 of them per row, moreover, only 3 upgrades can be chosen in a match. This means that you can upgrade your character to suit your playstyle, adding a lot of strategic depth into the game.

The ‘Nauts themselves all have relatively interesting backstories and quirks, which is evident in their voice-acted lines when you play them. Granted, a few of the voices of the ‘Nauts are a bit hit-and-miss, sometimes leaving me questioning why ‘Naut X has Voice Y because it doesn’t suit them, and some of the voice lines are blatant attempts to badly cram a few well known memes and references into the game because apparently ‘It’s funny’ (Some of the references are well done and funny in my opinion, but I would like to see SOME original dialogue as opposed to a sea of memes).

However, my major problem with this game lies in its’ online aspect, Ronimo execute this poorly, from the god-awful matchmaking which will leave you in a 1v3 against a full L1 premade, to the matches against players with over 400 ping, making it near impossible to dodge them, let alone win against them, ‘Awesomenauts’ knows how to make you rage online. In balance terms, the game is O.K at the moment, there are OP and UP ‘Nauts at the moment, which is only natural, but there are none which I currently consider stupidly unbalanced, despite the massive ‘Coco Nebulon’ Meta at the moment. The community, I feel, has also been gaining a lot of toxicity recently, but there isn’t much we can do, people have become more experienced and competitive since its’ release, and as a result, players become a lot angrier at new or inexperienced players who play the game for fun, which is a worrying and saddening trend in the once calm and collected community.

The paragraph above makes it sound like this game is absolutely awful. It makes me want to hate it, but I simply can’t. For every rage-inducing game, there is a genuinely fun game that draws you back in, and that makes this game fun and addictive as hell (Granted, I have had to take a break from it twice for about a month because I was sick of all the Bull). This is without a doubt my favourite game, and I think my hours show that, and I would recommend this to anyone interested in getting into MOBA's. But I would recommend that you bring a couple of friends along for the ride, it’s so much easier to deal with its’ BS together. If you want to go into it by yourself, fine. But trust me, you will need a lot of patience with it in order to see past its’ shortcomings, and appreciate it for what it is.

TL;DR: Love the ‘Saturday morning’ cartoon style, as well as the soundtrack. Very diverse roster of Nauts with interesting backstories. Balancing is a bit meh. Voice acting can be a bit uninspired. Bad matchmaking and network coding may result in rage inducing matches, but the rest of the game is good enough to help you see past its’ flaws.

Final score: 8/10

UPDATED: 4-11-2015

Facts: Before I start the review I want to state a fact, so that this review is not entirely based on my opinions. The player base went from 228,886 players in season 5 (Sep. 2013) to its current player base of 24,889 (4-11-2015) for a reason. That is a 920% decrease in the number of players. Also not all of the 24,889 players actually play the game on a regular basis, that is just the number of players that have played at least one match. If you check the reviews on steam most of the negative reviews are written by people who have 200-1000+ hours in the game and used to love playing it. Just keep that in mind before you buy this game.

Credentials: I have put over 580 hours into the game as of this review. I am a fairly high tier player and go back and forth between leagues 2 and 3, this means I have a good amount of experience in higher tier matches. 

First I will list the pros then the cons and then additional information. I do not consider the additional information to be a pro nor a con, I am just providing it for those who are still considering getting this game.

PROS:

-The graphic art and animations are great, and work well with the side-scrolling nature of this game.

-The characters are very unique and have cool abilities that give each character their own personality.

-The fighting in this game is very fun, it feels alot like smite had a baby with super mario bros.

-The abilities (upgrades) menu is very well done, and allows the player to counterbuild the enemy team.

-The leveling in this game is extremely simple. It is based off of collecting solar (currency) for player kills, turret kills, etc. and spending the solar in order to by abilities. This makes the game good for players that are new to this genre of game, and also provides enough complexity to entertain veterans to this genre.

-The maps are well made. Each map has a unique feature in its center. For example one map has reduced gravity, one has a giant worm that can kill you, one has an invisibility orb, and one has fire that turns on and off throughout the match.

CONS:

-The matchmaking system is terrible. As a league 2 player I was frequently matched against players that were league 6-7. There is a huge skill difference between leagues 6/7 and league 2, this made matches boring for me and frustrating for new players. Also the matchmaking system frequently puts players in matches that have already started. It is no fun to join a match in which your team is already loosing by a huge margine.

-The game is P2P. Players will constantly get matched against people with bad internet connection. This causes high latency and frequent packet loss. Since some characters do a ton of burst damage, if the player you are fighting has high latency, you can often be killed from 2-3 hit boxes away. The devs have talked about starting dedicated servers; however, they have been talking about it for over a year and still have not done it.

-Some characters are inherently better than other characters. This means that you will often play against the same characters over and over again until the next patch makes a different set characters better than the others.

-Players can die their way to victory. They do this by attacking the turret until they die, respawning and repeating over and over again. This is able to happen because certian characters do more damage to turrets than other characters. Also the abilities that these characters need to accomplish this are cheaper to get than other abilities.

Additional Information:

-Matches can last anywhere from 15-45 minutes.

-Each character has 4 rows of abilities with 6 abilities in each row. When you buy abilities in the match, you can have a maximum of 3 unique abilities in each row (only 3 out of the 6 for each row of abilities).

-The game is 3v3. This is the only option, there is no 2v2 or 5v5 like in some other MOBAs.

-You have to aim your abilities with your cursor (or controller), they do not auto hit on click (much like smite).

-The prestige system is optional. If you prestige, you loose all of your abilities and have to earn them back again. Some players will love this feature and some will hate it.

I hope that this review has been helpful, and has given you a better understanding of what the game is like. I want to emphatically state, that Awesomenauts is easily the most enjoyable Ronimo Games game I've seen/played. 
The game has so much potential to be far better than it is.
I would argue, at its peak, matches in Awesomenauts were much more satisfying than any game of League or DOTa could hope to provide. 

The idea of making a side scroller MOBA was brilliant. It addressed a huge problem with top down POV design in MOBAs.
It's a real pity Ronimo gave up on this killer IP in favor of working on other titles. 
If they had managed to successfully correct the myriad of critical issues with this game, it could had have been an amazing MOBA. Even with today's market, the game still has potential appeal, especially for younger players.

And now to rip into it:

The game is currently populated by very few players, often resulting in long wait times to match-make, and being forced into matchmaking scenarios that cause severe latency and lag to the point that some matches can be nearly unplayable is not uncommon. There is no work around for this and the easiest solution is to leave the match and que up again hoping for better luck with your match-makinng; you will still receive a leaver penalty for this. It's not uncommon for the game to seemingly randomly stall out for certain clients causing player characters to freeze in place while they are absolutely murdered by their hostile surroundings.

The player performance rating system is a total joke, and it's a pretty clearly an attempt to imitate the system League of Legends used; which was also terrible. 
Assist Kill tracking in particular works awfully, and yet, it is still the only stat in games that is worth taking even remotely seriously.

It's also very easy for games to spiral out of control due to highly volatile character match-ups and horrible balancing. At the competitive level, simply due to unlucky character match-ups, matches can be so one sided, that they are an insult to any player's time investment; regardless of overall skill.

The penalties enforced on players for toxic play styles and toxic social behavior are laughable and the systems in place to track are all but non-existant. 
Additionally, due to the lack of customer support and game integrity security for this game, cheating/hacking/modding is very easy to do and players have almost no recourse for stopping it. 
The cute little drop pod mini game for collecting solar is cute; but it's also punishing. So little solar (the in match store currency) is awarded over time, due to poor game design, that collecting the maximum solar on every player pod drop (especially the first one at match start) is critical to competitive play for certain characters.

The extra game mode play options are time vampires that play more like a baaad Mario Party mini game on the N64 than a modern game that released after the year 2000.

Before this game was free to play (retailing at just 10$) there was significantly more quality control of civility and legal play on the title. A big reason for this, is that banned accounts had to buy the game again on alternate accounts in order to keep negatively impacting the player base with cheating, toxic play, and toxic social behavior. Now a banned account is almost meaningless, as banned players can just remake an account, download the F2P game, load in their mods etc, and then resume their deplorable behavior. Making this game free to play and opening the door for micro-transactions was just a mistake.

The micro-transactions also were nearly a scam, as characters were wildly disproportionate in power level; especially late game characters. The majority of the characters available to play are borderline unplayable in competitive play with out lucky match ups due to wild discrepancies in over all power level of individual characters. I'm honestly surprised players didn't attempt a class action suit over Ronimo selling blatantly weaker characters for real world currency. 
Making nearly all characters skins micro-transaction only purchasable was also a poor decision.

Overall game performance with animations and individual skill hit-boxes is almost comically inaccurate, and it's baffling that the programmers kept on putting out broken content despite future nauts being increasingly unbalanced. No AAA game could ever get away with releasing a competitive game with multiplayer this broken. 

The game has a lot of flashing visuals and animation stuttering/rubber-banding from certain types of character attacks, especially blinding attacks and pushing/grabbing attacks (of which there are many of both), and it's is a serious accessibility issue.
If you have any kind of light sensitivity issues or seizure risks, please DO NOT play this game. It could pose a serious risk to your physical/neurological health.

Keyboard mouse controls are borderline unplayable and the controller commands on some characters struggle with input delay and non-intuitive motion responses to over all platforming. This is particularly bad with certain characters (nauts) when the player tries to drop down from a platform; an action that is a requirement for every map available.

Level design is also begging for a closer attention from a more skilled level design team. Some segments of the maps are so hard for certain champions (nauts) to navigate/platform through (due to differences in hit-box sizes, fall speeds, and control responsiveness, that they are literal death traps. 
Instant death traps also exist in the game and they are just as dumb as they sound. Instant death traps are the utter opposite of competitive play in a MOBA. The worm was a cool idea and it might've been fun, had it been designed well. The instant deaths by falling into the abyss and from the super creeps in the jungle however, are just inexcusable.

Possibly the only aspect of this game that still has appeal even in its current state is the art and animation design. The environmental art is stunning and the characters are wacky and memorable. This is as close as you can get to playing PVP game of a Saturday morning cartoon. 
The audio design has some pretty jamming tunes too and it's a pity they are wasted on this title. 

Ronimo if you are reading this, 
you really dropped the ball with this game in the end. Your player base deserved much better than what you ended up giving them.
Either take this game down or fix it. And please pay back your players for literally wasting their money on any player characters they purchased with real world money.

Okay, first thing's first: [u]I hate MOBAs.[/u]

I really hate them. The fantasy/myth/RPG styled theme, all the nonsense you need to cram into your brain faster than forgetting to study for a test and doing it last minute (I personally can tolerate that kind of stuff, but not with MOBAs) and the hostile communities make me hate them. Hate's a strong word, too. 

However, Awesomenauts is a significant turn for the better. Although the online multiplayer has its share of issues, Awesomenauts stands out from the rest and is what MOBAs should be like.

[h1]Graphics[/h1]

The graphics are cartoon-like, with a cheerful (yet dark at the same time) atmosphere. No fantasy stuff here, Awesomenauts is a sci-fi theme and that's something worth seeing after the same old MOBA. I love the visuals for the game, and I see nothing wrong with them.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]

The gameplay is simpler at first for the rookie MOBA player. Shoot stuff, (attacking without abilities has a bit of a meaning now, hooray!) use your abilities to get an edge over the other 'Nauts, and much more. But then, when you get into it, you'll start analyzing your playstyle to suit your needs with that 'Naut, how to take on the opponent in a one-on-one, and more. Although I did experience significant amounts of lag that costed me quite a few deaths and also really bad matchmaking, the gameplay is still solid to me.

[h1]Story[/h1]

The story is simple and straightforward. You play as an Awesomenaut (or Lonestar in the tutorial) and you need to destroy the enemy's Solar drill. Solar is crucial to your employer for an unknown reason, and you need to destroy the drill so you hinder the enemy's Solar supply. MOBAs are known for their lore, and although this game lacks lore compared to other MOBAs, Awesomenauts doesn't fit in the category of a fantasy/RPG world like this.

[h1]Audio[/h1]

The audio is probably the key point to the game. The music (especially the theme song, just play the trailer if you haven't done so already) is outstanding, and the themes really get into your head. My personal favorite themes are Froggy G, Yuri, and the new character Scoop. The voice actors did an OUTSTANDING job with playing the characters and don't seem all bold or shrouded like most MOBAs do. Each one has their own personality that makes them unique from the others, and if I'm not mistaken, popular Youtuber TotalBiscuit even voiced one of the characters (Vinnie and Spike I believe) which I found pretty interesting. The audio overall to this game is near perfection, and I feel empty inside without those "[i]awesome[/i]" songs.

[h1]Replayability[/h1]

The replayability is pretty massive. I don't want to touch up here much because it's a MOBA. Its easy to get hundreds of hours logged onto a MOBA.

For one thing though, Awesomenauts has some major pros that don't fit into any of the five main categories. The developers are dedicated, for one. They constantly release updates and even do some charity work. Check out Lonestar's Private Mels (?) skin. A kid came in from the Make-a-Wish Foundation and made his own skin for his favorite Awesomenaut. The updates keep on rolling in, and the most recent (as of this review anyway, 2.7 in case you're wondering) introduces Scoop, buffed every character in the game, gained a new main menu, and so much more it's better I keep my mouth shut. One more thing though that sets Awesomenauts apart from the rest is that the community is [b]much, much, MUCH nicer compared to the other MOBAs.[/b] You don't get yelled at for screwing up, you actually GET help when you need it, and so Awesomenauts makes me feel comfortable when I get on.

[h1]Verdict[/h1]

In the end, Awesomenauts may be in my least favorite game genre, but who cares? Awesomenauts still got a thumbs-up from me. Aside from a few online flaws, Awesomenauts is a game that fails to disappoint me, and is one amazing adventure not worth missing.

This is a hard game to love, but I do. I've sunk far too much time into it to say I don't love it. It can be extremely fun but also very infuriating. 

It's meant to be a casual side-scrolling Moba / Dota-clone and it does that very well, but when I say casual, I mean super casual. Not caring about winning and game-breaking issues casual. 

I can handle losing just fine and I couldn't care less about ranking. Being out-played and out-maneuvered comes with any online game. You play until you get better. What I can't handle is losing because you can go 1v3 or the drop-in / drop-out system forcing you to be always down a player because someone forgot they left the oven on and the next person just got a call, so your 3rd is constantly on their way to fight. Or the terrible matchmaking making you join a game where everyone has 300+ ping (yes you can set the game to find only local players but the player base is so small I've had that take 15+ minutes. And then the game is force-started because someone is too impatient). 

There's issues involving lag even in local region games that have been around since game launch and continue to persist and will forever persist, because the game uses a p2p hosting model instead of a dedicated server. That cost cutting measure is simply awful and I've been dropped out of MANY games where the host decides to leave and we can't all get connected to the new host, sometimes resulting in the entire match being scrapped. 

I've played the game since almost launch, contributed far too much money to the expansion kickstarter and bought some DLC I didn't care about just to support the devs.  But I've also uninstalled 6-8 times and quit for months at a time because all the issues got to be too much. 

I usually come back after a big patch rollout hoping some more issues are solved, but more often than not it's simply some unless flair added to the GUI and some balance changes which I can rarely understand the reasoning behind. 

I've ragged on it a lot and I'm not giving it a thumbs up (in its current state), but I do recommend picking it up, maybe on sale and giving it a shot. Maybe it will have most of my issues with it fixed and if not, at least you can get some good hours out of it.

I really wish they took these characters and made actual games with them instead.

MOBA isn't a terrible look, though. When you play on your own, it's a very arcade-like MOBA. Every skill of every character has at least two distinct build paths and maybe more depending on how you decide to cross-build them. Provided, most characters seem like they'd have either specific counterpick builds or one catch-all build for most situations.

Every character, in single-player, lets you either spread your upgrades across your three skills and base stats, or you can hyper-focus on one skill. At base for most characters, every skill is in its ideal usable form... although some characters are exceptions. Going Lonestar without tri-namite (+24% damage) seems like you're shooting yourself in the food. Smiles without the inscribed lighter also feels just categorically worse.

However!

Playing with friends sucks. See, the way the matchmaking is coded, 3 player co-op necessitates you get sweaty. You'll be playing against other 3-player teams, and they'll be competitive. If you play like you're all asocial jerks playing alone, you lose, end of story. Not a little, but a lot, almost all the time. Unless you get lucky and get a disorganized wreck for an enemy team, then you might break even or even win, but that's all luck, so it doesn't make you feel like you're accomplishing anything, even if you're trashing people. 

This is especially unkind to new players, especially considering the number of 'nauts and the free-to-play currency system. Why do you gain it so slowly? Is this a freakin' mobile game? Why's someone gotta do like 50 matches to get a new freakin' hero? They're restricted so hard from build choices and character choices.

The issue with losing a lot is that players can't experiment and learn. Bots don't teach them the proper aggression, patience, game economy or flow, but players will snowball after your team of incompetent non-MOBA gamers make their very first mistake. And then you, if you have any experience with just Awesomenauts, will want to tear their heads off. You know they're not being provided the right feedback to learn from their mistakes, and even if you know how they failed, you can't just magically gain control of their arms and eyes and give them that experience. And then that directly impacts on you. You have to play ultra-safe, pick ultra-safe, do it all real carefully, 'cause builds that might work if enabled by the single-player environment or by a good team of people carrying you simply aren't gonna work here. Not when you gotta look after teammates feeding 0/15/0 or 2/10 or 0/4 or 0/8 who are allergic to team fights, ganks or looking at the mini-map. 

But then you die for the first time. Maybe you just got ganked by an assassin at a bad moment. Maybe the whole team ganked you while your friends were off being dead or clueless and you went "wow, if only my team could ever do that." But now that you've died one time, you know it's all over. Nah, your death didn't cause it, it's just a warning of how it's about to go down. You're not getting stats or economy fast enough, and your teammates can't bless you with a strategic comeback. Meanwhile you'll probably end up with, say, one or two upgrades between now and when you lose.

And this was supposed to be played on a couch with controllers with your IRL mates at one point? Really? [i]Really?[/i] This is the furthest thing you can get from suitable for that, even if the graphical design and tone fully checks out.

Even when I'm on the upperhand of a snowballing, stompy game, I don't like it. It's just not that satisfying when I don't feel like my opponents can fight back. It's like I didn't win because I played better, or even because my team cumulatively made less mistakes, but because the result of the game was locked-in. Either we played really well in the first five minutes, or we just got lucky in the first five minutes and now the other team just can't and now we get to wail on them. It's almost like the game is designed to make you think you can sustain and hold a comeback, but it's very unlikely and heavily discouraged by the format.

I think this's the real reason the game is dying. I think, in some ways, league is actually better with this sort of thing. But the singleplayer's pretty cool.

Even though I enjoy it, I can't recommend it. Too much jank, neglect and age. MOBAs are already kinda lame, but competition and marketing and the social element keep the format afloat. Despite that, I think league is unironically a funner party game. Single-player Awesomenauts is categorically not a party game, though it is a fun arcade-like game.

The game is fun, the music is fantastic, and the characters are memorable. You get a remixed version of your character's theme if you get a killing spree, and those really make you feel like a badass.

The artstyle is great too, nothing really looks bad, and everything definitely looks like it belongs in the same universe.

There's a good variety of maps, which helps keep the game fresh.

The only issue this game has is it's relatively small playerbase, which can result in matchmaking being a tad unfair sometimes: one team might stomp another quite easily. However, with Awesomenauts becoming F2P, that will very likely improve. Also, matchmaking is surprisingly short despite the small playerbase.

One thing I haven't seen other people bring up is the benefits of being a 3v3 game, compared to something like League of Legends or DotA. With this game being 3v3, there is a far lower chance of there being angry people shouting insults at you. There are only 5 other people who could be flamers, whereas 5v5 games have 9. I've noticed that I am far less likely to get yelled at if I do poorly in this game.

Another benefit is that if you want to not queue up with random people, it's far easier to assemble a full team out of your friends. After all, you only need two friends to get a full team: whereas in a 5v5 game, you would need four friends willing to play with you.

Is this game fun, Well yes. BUT there are somethings that need to change in order for this game to truely be a good game. 

Pros.
The game perfectly captures the moba spirit, but in a fast paced action platformer. Don't like RTS style constant clicking? Think there's not enough action in Dota or league of legends? This game has it.

Voice acting and soundtrack are great.
artstyle is nice and fresh

The game IS fun.

Negatives.

This game can not be competitive yet. There are numerous reasons why, but let's start off with the worst offenders.

1. There is no strategy to picking a character. None. There isn't a draft, so you can't see what the other team is going to pick. It's like Blind pick in league of legends. There's a reason for that mode not being ranked. If the other team happens to pick a character that counters yours, you're screwed the entire game. 

I propose something like league of legends. Each team can ban 1 character, and they take turns picking their characters while the one they picked is shown to both teams. Until this is implemented, If you are looking for a serious competition, go look elsewhere.

2. The Paywall.
What Paywall? The expansion. I'm fine with them having an expansion. That isn't the issue. Here's the issue. Almost all of the expansion characters have a attack that passes through the turrets. Normally, you can use the turret as a shield to take some damage while you fight off the enemy team. A lot of the characters in the expansion have attacks that can go through said turret. nibbs, Penny, Ted McPain (in levels that have the turrets on top of the jungle area), sentry x58 has an attack that draws you in from behind the turret. You see where I'm going with this? Ok. So there are characters that can get you behind the turret. There must be one that can in the normal game too, right? Yeah, there is. One. Coco. So if you have the expansion, you can poke the heck out of anyone behind the turret, but if you just have the base game? Just pray there's a coco on your team or you're screwed because you can't touch them. 

3. Joining late games.
The game has bots take over after someone leaves. That's awesome and well needed in other mobas. You know what isn't awesome? Other players can then join the game and replace these bots. I've had numerous times where I'd join a game, only to find out all the turrets were gone for us and the whole team had rage quit so I'm the only one there. A garenteed lose. Gee, thanks. Unfortunately this happens WAY to often. You get screwed just for wanting to play the game! If people still want that feature, fine. Put a switch in there that you can click and say "I only want to join NEW games. NOT games in progress." This sucks.

4. Disconnections. The game gives you a penalty for quiting the game. This is good. Unfortunately, You can't rejoin games that you have disconnected from. Internet goes down for a second? Congrats, you are now punished when you start another game.  Game crashes? Punished. Fair, right? You should be able to rejoin games that you we disconnected from. Simple as that.

Summary:
This game is fun. I always have a good match or two when playing. But, because of these problems, I can't recommend this game. These issues need to be fixed before this game is good enough to recommend to anyone.
